ai_summary: The Township of Admaston/Bromley Council voted to adopt a new bylaw (2023-61) to regulate backyard chickens. Concurrently, the Council approved an amendment to the Fees and Charges By-Law (2023-62) to establish a permit fee for backyard chickens.

The municipality is endorsing the proposed heritage designation of 6673 Highway 35 (the Pattie House) under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act. This action is a direct response to amendments introduced by Bill 23, the More Homes Built Faster Act, which mandates municipalities to designate listed properties or remove them from the Heritage Register.

The municipality is informing the public of an upcoming meeting on May 11, 2026, to discuss the Development Charges Background Study and the proposed Development Charges By-law. This public meeting is a required step in the process of establishing or updating the municipality's development charge policies.

The municipality formally considered an addendum to its 2024 Development Charges Background Study at its July 18, 2024 hybrid meeting. This action reflects the Council's review of updated information directly related to the municipality's development charge policies.

The municipality is actively undertaking a Development Charges Background Study. This study is a mandated precursor to potentially updating or enacting a new Development Charges Bylaw, which outlines fees for new development to fund growth-related capital costs.
The municipality is actively developing new policy regarding land use. Specifically, a draft Site Alteration Bylaw is under consideration.
